task: Create a responsive ecommerce homepage for a small-batch coffee brand called Northline Coffee. The primary goal is to help a first-time visitor understand the roast collection and choose a coffee without feeling overwhelmed.
research_evidence: Use a simple product taxonomy: roast intensity, tasting notes, and brew method.
Product cards should expose price, size, and a clear purchase action without forcing a detail-page visit.
Avoid decorative coffee imagery that pushes the product name and purchase action below the fold.

design_spec.information_architecture: Header with brand, Shop, Subscription, About, and cart; hero with one featured roast and one CTA; three roast-category cards; featured product grid; subscription value proposition; compact footer.
design_spec.layout: Warm off-white canvas with a dark espresso header and a restrained orange accent. Use a 12-column desktop grid and one-column mobile flow. Keep hero copy to a maximum of 60 words and place the featured product image beside it on desktop, above the CTA on mobile.
design_spec.typography: Use a high-contrast serif only for the hero heading and a readable system sans for body copy, labels, prices, and navigation. Body text must remain at least 16px.
components: product card with price and tasting notes
responsive_rules: At <= 720px collapse navigation into a menu button.
At <= 720px stack hero content and keep the primary CTA visible before the product image.
Product grid changes from 3 columns to 2 columns at 900px and 1 column at 560px.
interaction_states: cart badge updates without layout shift
menu button exposes and closes navigation
design_spec.accessibility: Use semantic landmarks, labelled navigation, visible focus styles, alt text, sufficient color contrast, and buttons instead of clickable divs.

task: Design a desktop and mobile analytics dashboard for a climate operations SaaS. The user is a facilities manager who needs to spot energy anomalies and decide what to investigate next within 30 seconds.
constraints: do not use red for every alert
research_evidence: A dashboard should lead with the decision the user needs to make, not a wall of equally weighted metrics.
Separate status, trend, and action: a number alone is not an explanation.
Use color as a secondary signal and include text labels or icons for alert severity.

design_spec.information_architecture: Persistent left navigation with Overview, Buildings, Energy, Reports, and Settings. Main content starts with date range and building filters, then an anomaly summary, trend chart, building table, and a right-side action panel.
design_spec.layout: Two-column dashboard at desktop: 1fr main content plus 320px action rail. At <= 900px the action rail moves below the main content. Cards share one surface, 16px radius, and consistent 24px padding.
design_spec.typography: Use a readable sans-serif. Dashboard title 32px, card title 16px, metric 30px, supporting text 13–14px. Never encode meaning only through color.
responsive_rules: At <= 900px move the action rail below the chart and make the sidebar collapsible.
At <= 768px turn the table into stacked building cards or allow controlled horizontal scrolling with an accessible label.
Keep filters usable without wrapping into an unreadable multi-line toolbar.
interaction_states: anomaly row expands to show evidence
empty state when no anomalies exist
design_spec.accessibility: Use landmarks, button labels, aria-expanded for collapsible controls, text severity labels, table headers, and a non-color status indicator.

task: Create a mobile-first public website for a community science festival. The goal is to help families find an event, understand age suitability, and reserve a free place in under two minutes.
research_evidence: Event pages should surface date, time, location, age range, and availability before the long description.
Families often browse on mobile while travelling, so the primary booking action should remain visible without excessive scrolling.
Do not rely on abstract event titles alone; explain the activity in one sentence.

design_spec.information_architecture: Header with festival mark and menu; hero with date and city; filter chips for day, age, and event type; event cards with time, location, age, availability, and reserve CTA; short about section; footer with access information.
design_spec.layout: Bright paper background, deep navy text, coral and teal accents. Use a two-column event grid above 800px and single-column cards below. Each event card has a strong time block on the left and content on the right.
design_spec.typography: Use a friendly geometric sans-serif with bold headings and generous line-height. Do not use all caps for essential event details.
responsive_rules: At <= 600px keep the date and reserve button visible near the top of every card.
Filters become horizontally scrollable chips with a visible label and no clipped text.
The footer remains readable without tiny text.
interaction_states: reserve button loading and success state
no-results state with clear reset action
design_spec.accessibility: Use semantic headings, labelled filter controls, descriptive event text, visible focus styles, and clear button labels such as Reserve a free place.
